text: Roughly how much faster is a spike from a photonic (excitable-laser) neuron than a biological spike?
choices: About 8 orders of magnitude faster: a biological spike lasts ~1 ms while an excitable-laser spike is ~1-10 ps
They occur at essentially the same speed
explanation: A biological spike is about 1 ms while an excitable semiconductor-laser neuron produces ~1-10 ps spikes, roughly eight orders of magnitude faster (Nahmias et al. 2013). The physical basis is fast optical dynamics (photon lifetime ~ps, carrier lifetime ~ns), so the gap is far larger than 10x or 100x.
